invariantResults.name: INV-6 autoAnnihilate liveness against an honest strategy

counterexample.result: Against the real ERC4626YieldStrategy over a yielded vault (1.2467 assets/share), a caller owed exactly 1 wei of Antimatter has netWanted == 1; convertToShares(1) == 0, the redeem delivers 0, and require(received > 0 ...) at :588 reverts 'StableStaker: exit shortfall' - a message that accuses an honest strategy of lying. Self-heals after further accrual. Occurred 50/17,729 (0.28%) of gate-closed attempts, 46 of them on the real ERC4626 pool and 0 on the idle pool.
counterexample.scalingLaw: The double round-down in _disposeShares loses up to one share's worth of assets while the allowance is 2 + netFloor/10_000, so the floor fails whenever assetsPerShare > 2 + netFloor/10_000. Demonstrated at an (unrealistic) 1247 assets/share in Run17_ExitShortfallDust::test_scalingLaw_highSharePriceBreaksTheFloorForOrdinaryExits. Not a live finding at stablecoin-autopool prices, but it is why the flat EXIT_ROUNDING_ALLOWANCE = 2 is load-bearing and must not be reduced.

measurements.name: underwater buffer-funded surplus (profile obs. 1)
measurements.value: 202767365267183752539 raw units (202.77 DAI2) paid to ONE caller as `surplus` out of the SHARED idle buffer in a single autoAnnihilate, with a 1.5% exit slippage and the strategy 2% below par
measurements.mechanism: _routeExit:1186-1195 returns `gross` verbatim rather than `netWanted`, so the caller pockets gross - netWanted at :609 having incurred no actual AMM haircut. Reached 6,387 times across the two campaigns.

fixtureCaveats: MockERC4626Vault is OZ's reference ERC4626 plus a donation hook and charges NO withdrawal/exit fee, whereas a real Tokemak-style autopool may. Every conclusion about the FEE-BLINDNESS of previewExitFor is therefore NOT load-bearing here; the ROUNDING conclusions (INV-6) are, because they come from the real ERC4626YieldStrategy over a real OZ vault.

MockYieldStrategy (pool 2) was checked: relinquishPrincipal has a real body that writes principal down. relinquishPrincipalAsOwner IS an empty stub, but StableStakerV2 never calls it, so no result depends on it.

Pool 2's `previewExitFor` mirrors its own `withdraw` byte-for-byte, i.e. it is an HONEST market strategy. It is therefore laxer than a real AMM-routed strategy in one direction (no execution variance); the 4 pool-2 shortfall hits are not load-bearing and the pool-1 (real ERC4626) hits are.
The Medusa rig runs gate-closed only, so claim's mint at :449 has zero coverage there. Foundry's gate-open campaign covers it (21,258 successful claims).
